title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 40–42): Grothendieck is axiomatizing what he calls a 'classification' 𝒜. It carries a relation ≪, a lattice-like ordered set Σ of 'supports' (with ≤, a bottom element ∅_Σ, meets ∩, and a disjointness relation |·|), and for each X ∈ 𝒜 a set X̃ ordered with a largest element. On p.40 he defines the 'spatial unfolding' Dép(X) = {X'^0 | X' ∈ X̃} ⊂ Σ_conv ⊂ Σ. The elements X'^0 are mutually disjoint, nonempty and in bijection with X̃. Dép(X) carries the order transported from X̃, not the order of Σ. A plausible modern reading: X is a closed 'stratified' object, X̃ is the poset of its strata (closure order), and X'^0 is the open stratum. Then Dép(X) is the decomposition of the support of X into disjoint pieces, indexed by the stratum poset.

This page: suppose X ≪ Y. There is a canonical increasing map φ: X̃ → Ỹ with x' ≪̊ φ(x') for each x'. Translated into unfoldings, this becomes an increasing map ψ: Dép(X) → Dép(Y) with S ≤ ψ(S) in Σ: each piece of X lies inside a piece of Y. ψ is uniquely determined by this property. Suppose S ≤ T and S ≤ T' with T, T' ∈ Dép(Y) and S ≠ ∅_Σ. If T ≠ T', then T |·| T', so T ∩ T' = ∅. Hence S ≤ ∅, so S = ∅, a contradiction.

The next page turns this into a necessary condition R for X ≪ Y: every piece of Dép X is contained in some (necessarily unique) piece of Dép Y, and the induced map is increasing. The strict relation X ≪̊ Y is characterized by X^0 ≤ Y^0 in addition. A classification is then called 'spatial' when R is also sufficient. So the page serves the program of deciding when the abstract combinatorial relation ≪ is faithfully realized by containment of supports. In stratified-space language: when 'X ≪ Y' is equivalent to 'the stratification of X refines into that of Y'.
errors: Minor: the uniqueness argument tacitly needs Σ to have meets compatible with ≤ (S ≤ T, T' ⇒ S ≤ T∩T'), and needs disjointness to mean T∩T' = ∅. Both appear to be among the standing axioms, so the argument is correct given them.

Potential confusion, not an error: Dép(X) has a 'largest element' X^0 only for the order transported from X̃. In Σ the elements of Dép(X) are pairwise disjoint, so not comparable. The page is careful to say ψ is increasing for the transported order and S ≤ ψ(S) for Σ's order.

ideas.what: Unfolding Dép(X) of an object into pairwise disjoint 'open pieces' X'^0 indexed by the poset X̃, and the induced map ψ: Dép X → Dép Y characterized by S ≤ ψ(S)
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of a stratified space into open strata indexed by its stratum poset; a map of stratified objects sending strata into strata (refinement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom/Mather (stratifications); poset-stratified spaces in Lurie's Higher Algebra appendix
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6) discusses tame topology and stratified structures in a related spirit, but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the stratum containing a nonempty piece, via disjointness of distinct strata
Program (completed next page): call a classification 'spatial' when the abstract relation ≪ is exactly detected by containment of unfolded supports (condition R)
ideas.modern_name: Geometric realizability / faithfulness of an abstract incidence structure by a stratified-space model

missed.claim: An abstract axiomatics of 'classifications', with supports Σ, unfoldings Dép(X) and the notion of a 'spatial' classification (where ≪ is equivalent to piecewise containment of unfoldings), appears to be developed only in these 1986 notes. Its precise scope and relation to stratified spaces / tame topology are not documented in the literature.
missed.quote: En termes de déploiements, on peut interpréter φ par une application croissante ψ : Dép(X) → Dép(Y) satisfaisant ∀S ∈ Dép X, S ≤ ψ(S)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with poset-stratified spaces and exit-path/constructible formalisms, where morphisms are required to send strata into strata. It might clarify what Grothendieck intended for a combinatorial foundation of 'tame' geometry. The content on this page alone is elementary, though.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an elementary but clean step in an otherwise undocumented 1986 axiomatics of 'classifications' and their 'spatial unfoldings'. The mathematics itself (strata-to-strata maps, uniqueness via disjointness) is routine. The interest lies only in the unpublished framework it belongs to.
transcription_corrections: Line 'x' ≪̊ φ(x')': the image shows φ(X') written and then struck through and replaced by 'y' ≝ φ(X')'; the variables are capital X', Y' rather than x', y'.
The struck words before 'S ≤ T, T'' read roughly 'pour une' / 'peut-on', crossed out; the intended sentence is 'car si S ≤ T, T', avec T, T' ∈ Dép(Y), on a T = T''.
Parenthetical: '(et ceci, pourvu seulement que S soit un élément de Σ, ≠ ∅_Σ)'.
Last line: 'En effet, si T ≠ T', on a T |·| T',' (disjointness relation).
